$comment: Shared state for ONE work-graph run. Lives at .graph/runs/<run-id>/state.json. Every node reads this on start and appends to its OWN key on finish - the builder writes its own builders.<slice> key, including the branch it worked on. Never rewrite another node's key. Every node key carries written_by, naming the node that wrote it: that is the ONLY record of authorship this file has, and without it 'never rewrite another node's key' is unverifiable - an orchestrator hand-writing all six keys is indistinguishable from six nodes doing their jobs. verify-state.py --audit checks it. This file is the edge: it is how context crosses between agents that cannot see each other.

decisions_for_gate.topic: Provider API changes (deliberate, listed) and call-result routing
decisions_for_gate.recommend: LinkContextValue adds: inbox (InboxItem[] as held), outbox (Record of item_id to OutboxEntry), canAnswer (scopes include answer), answer(a: permission or question Answer), cancelAnswer(item_id), retryAnswer(item_id), dismissAnswer(item_id). inboxCount changes meaning to pending permission and question items (what the phone lists). decisions_for_gate.recommend: In memory only, in the controller. It survives link drops, network changes and backgrounding, which is what 'queued while offline' needs for a host on the LAN or tailnet; it does not survive the app process dying, and the queued copy says so ('Closing the app drops it'). A persisted answer would be sent after a restart into a desktop state the person never saw. No new dependency, no new build, OTA-safe.
alternatives: SecureStore, one key per queued answer: the repo caps a value at 2048 bytes (store.ts:18) while a question answer can be 32 x 4096 bytes, so big answers would be refused offline; SecureStore cannot enumerate keys, so an index is needed. Possible later.

expo-file-system (npx expo install): a new native module, so a new build under runtimeVersion fingerprint (app.json:61-63), and answer text on disk in plaintext unless encrypted under a SecureStore key. Not for A2.

decisions_for_gate.recommend: Sensitive, not a secret in the CLAUDE.md sense (that rule names pairing keys and tokens). It can hold anything typed (a password, a path), so in A2 it is never persisted, never logged, never put in an error or copy string, and lives only in the controller outbox and the in-memory drafts. If a later milestone persists it (A5 notification actions, say), it goes to expo-secure-store or an encrypted file, never AsyncStorage.
alternatives: Treat it as a secret now: same A2 behaviour, and it forces SecureStore for any future cache. Fine too.
Treat it as plain data: would allow AsyncStorage later. No.

decisions_for_gate.topic: A queued answer vs the world (reconcile)
decisions_for_gate.recommend: Checked on every snapshot and inbox-updated, before any send. Item resolved and not expired while queued: answered ('This request was already answered.'), not sent. Item expired: expired (desktop wording), not sent, terminal. Item missing from a snapshot: gone, not sent. On reconnect the outbox flushes only after the new snapshot is applied. Results: ok = sent (cleared when the item resolves); already_answered = answered; failed while the held item is expired = expired; failed otherwise = failed, text kept, Try again; forbidden = refused, with the no-scope copy; bad_request or an unknown code = failed, the code shown as plain text. Revoked or Forget empties the outbox (the host drops queued calls on revoke anyway). Nothing terminal is retried automatically, so an expired item cannot loop.
alternatives: Send queued answers regardless and let the host refuse: same end state with needless calls and a flash of Sending. No.
Ask before sending queued answers after a reconnect: one more tap for the common case. Possible if wanted.

decisions_for_gate.recommend: One call id per attempt: 'a-' + 16 random bytes in hex (34 bytes, under the 128 cap) from deps.random, the one randomness source. The same id is reused for the automatic resend after a drop and for Try again from unconfirmed, so the host's 256-id cache (conn.rs:40, kept across reconnects) applies it once and replays the first result. A new id only for Try again after a definitive failed, since a replay would return the same failure. A failed result to a resend of the same id (the host's 'that call is still running' case, conn.rs:545) goes unconfirmed, decided by the attempt number, never by message text. After a host restart the cache is gone, but the item is then expired in the new snapshot, so nothing is resent.
alternatives: A fresh id per send: a resend after a drop gets already_answered for its own answer. No.
An id derived from item_id: a deliberate second try after a failure would replay the failure. No.

findings.issue: A definite failure can be hidden forever. Suppose attempt 1 runs on the host and fails, for example send_through fails or there is an internal error. The host caches Done(Err(failed)) (core/src/link/conn.rs:149, :557-558). If the link drops before the result arrives, the resend with the same id gets the cached failed, which attempt>1 maps to unconfirmed. Try again from unconfirmed keeps the id (outbox.ts:81), so it gets the same replay and goes unconfirmed again, every time. dismiss (outbox.ts:90) and cancel refuse unconfirmed, and answer() refuses while it is held (controller.ts answer). The user cannot clear it or answer differently until the item resolves, expires or disappears. A scratch test reproduced this over 3 Try agains. It does not loop on its own, since nothing auto-retries. This follows A2-G7 and the slice intent to the letter, so it is not a builder blocker. Possible fixes: allow Dismiss on unconfirmed (s3 copy), or mint a new id after a second failed on the same id.

A builder choice: unconfirmed frees the one-in-flight slot, because flush checks only 'sending'. So a timed-out call and the next answer can be outstanding at the host together. I judge this acceptable. The same item can never get two ids this way: answer() is blocked while unconfirmed, and Try again reuses the id. Different items are independent, and the host allows 8 calls per connection. The scratch test confirmed that a late result for the freed call does not clear the next call's timer. builders.s2 reports deviation 'none' for this; the builder notes mention it.

clearTimers now calls linkDown, which calls set(). So dispose() (controller.ts:190, through stopLink) notifies listeners after disposed=true and before listeners.clear() whenever an entry is sending. That is one extra emit to a provider that is unmounting. Harmless today.

pair() does not empty the outbox. Queued entries from a previous host carry into a new pairing. They become 'gone' after the new host's snapshot, because their item ids are absent, and they are never sent. That is safe, but they show as 'no longer on <host>' under the new host's name.

Missing-item rows are appended in outbox insertion order (oldest entry first), not newest first; there is no created_at to sort by. Placing them after the pending rows is sensible; an outbox timestamp would be needed to order them.

clearDrafts empties the store but a mounted item screen keeps its useState copy. If a revoke lands while the screen is open, the text stays in component memory (not shown, since the item leaves the inbox); after a re-pair to the same host and the same item id, the stale text would render while the store is blank. In memory only, no disk; edge case.

pair() clears drafts on entry, so a pairing attempt that fails or is cancelled also drops the old host's drafts. Consistent with s2's emptying of the outbox at the same point and within 'Forget, revoke and pair'.
